newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end up in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end up in thin trade.

text.p: Rubber futures closed mostly higher on Monday in thin trade as higher prices in Japan buoyed the market, dealers said.

"There was some buying for RSS3 rubber by local dealers and some foreign houses in the afternoon. But the volume is still thin and the market only firmed largely because of higher Japanese prices," a trader for a foreign brokerage house said.
Prices of Tokyo's benchmark August contract closed 2.1 yen up to 153.6 yen.
"The volume was not encouraging. Buying interest was just not there," another dealer said.
Total volume of RSS3 rubber trader reached 900 tonnes, up from Friday's 400 tonnes, but meagre when compared with the 7,230 tonnes traded last Thursday.

At around 0945 GMT, most active May RSS3 was seen at 123.00-125.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 122.75 cents. April RSS1 was seen at 173.00-175.00 Singapore cents (US$1.21-$1.22) a kg from 173.00 cents.
May TSR20 was seen at 169.00-171.00 Singapore cents (US$1.18-$1.19) a kg from the previous 170.00 cents.
